subject: Life Skills
title: Carbon Monoxide: The Silent Killer
description: A short lesson to help you apply Carbon Monoxide: The Silent Killer.

hook.text: Carbon monoxide is invisible and odorless. Over 400 Americans die from it in their homes each year.

buildup.text: CO comes from gas stoves, heaters, fireplaces, and running cars in attached garages.

discovery.text: Symptoms mimic the flu: headaches, dizziness, and nausea. Victims often don't realize the cause in time.

twist.text: Opening windows helps but doesn't fix the source. A leaking furnace will keep producing CO indefinitely.

climax.text: Install CO detectors on every level. If the alarm sounds, leave immediately and call from outside.

punchline.text: You can't smell it. Let the detector do that job.

quiz.question: Why is carbon monoxide especially dangerous?
options: It causes explosions in enclosed spaces
It is invisible and odorless with flu-like symptoms
It only affects people with breathing problems
